route.name: Rio Grande - Ute Mountain Run
route.stateAssignment: New Mexico; upstream Lobatos Bridge launch is in Colorado, and the route continues through New Mexico to Lee Trail.

qualification.demandAndDistinctness: The named 24-mile Ute Mountain float is a distinct upper Rio Grande corridor not covered by the Taos-area route cards. It uses BLM-designated launch/take-out locations and is not a synthetic endpoint combination.
qualification.scoring: BLM recommends at least 300 cfs. American Whitewater's reach-specific study places 600-2,000 cfs in the optimal user-preference range; this route uses a conservative 600-1,500 cfs preferred band and 2,000 cfs upper scoring guard due to the route guide's advanced/expert caution above about 1,500 cfs. Direct gauge 08251500 is at the upstream launch. Values are planning cues, not safety guarantees.
qualification.access: Lobatos Bridge BLM ramp coordinate is 37.078611, -105.756389 from the route guide and bridge description. Lee Trail is a BLM-designated take-out. The listed American Whitewater access feature coordinate (36.864, -105.705) falls about 303 ft outside the NHD water trace and outside mapped water polygons, so the route map instead uses the nearest in-channel Rio Grande point at the designated Lee Trail reach end (36.864295, -105.706712). Treat this as an in-channel marker; trail/parking are on the rim after the steep primitive quarter-mile carry.
qualification.safety: Reviewed fitted PFD, rescue/communication/navigation gear, cold-water and wind controls, blind-drop scouting, remote rescue exposure, seasonal closure and advance reservation. The reservation source material differs on daily launch cap, so the card says to confirm the current cap with BLM.
qualification.camping: campingClassification=none. BLM reports very few practical camps and steep rim access; this is a day route, with any established campground use treated as separate logistics.
qualification.gallery: Added BLM public-domain Ute Mountain / upper Rio Grande gorge photo from Wikimedia Commons. Caption identifies same-river/reach-area context, not a current condition or endpoint image.
qualification.geometry: Generated route-scoped canonical geometry from the named USGS NHD Rio Grande flowline. Trace is one line / 2,400 points with maximum endpoint offset 35 ft; targeted hydrography audit passes 2/2 endpoints (0 review, suspicious, failure or unknown).
qualification.consolidation: No duplicate identifier or same-corridor route existed. This upper route terminates at Lee Trail and does not duplicate the separate Taos Box or lower-gorge access chains.

followUp: Before deployment, verify the current launch cap, reservation availability, road access, wind and live gauge. Full state geometry bundle regeneration and gallery/safety audits are in progress.
